unicorn/no-array-for-each.why: enabled bare in production; Array#forEach with a callback, with the for-of loop the rule asks for sitting above it as a control

unicorn/prefer-array-find.why: enabled bare in production; `filter(...)[0]` with a `.find()` control so the row cannot be pinned by an always-reporting file

unicorn/prefer-set-has.why: enabled bare in production; neither tool reports a lone membership test, so the array is read by two `.includes()` calls and the finding lands on its declaration

unicorn/prefer-set-size.why: enabled bare in production; the inline `[...new Set(x)].length` is the only shape ESLint reports under @typescript-eslint/parser, because its isSet() needs the variable definition's kind and typescript-eslint's scope manager omits it, while oxlint also reports the `const set = new Set()` and Array.from forms -- the fixture therefore stays on the shared shape

unicorn/prefer-string-replace-all.why: enabled bare in production; a global regex passed to String#replace, with a replaceAll control below it

unicorn/prefer-at.why: tripwire for the rule oxlint enables and production ESLint does not, at default options: oxlint does emit two identical diagnostics for the single `slice(-1)[0]` in raw --format json (open upstream double-report), but the harness counts unique (file, line, rule) so the row is plain parity at 1 and the doubling is only visible in oxlint's own error total
